title: Sweet tartlet shells (individual tart crusts)
name: Sweet tartlet shells (individual tart crusts)

ingredients.item: plain flour (all-purpose flour)
ingredients.name: plain flour (all-purpose flour)

ingredients.item: soft icing sugar (powdered sugar) (, sifted (Note 1))
ingredients.name: soft icing sugar (powdered sugar) (, sifted (Note 1))

ingredients.item: almond meal (ground almonds) (, not almond flour (Note 2))
ingredients.name: almond meal (ground almonds) (, not almond flour (Note 2))

ingredients.item: cooking salt / kosher salt
ingredients.name: cooking salt / kosher salt

ingredients.item: / 7 tbsp  unsalted butter (, unsalted, softened, cut into 1cm / 0.4" cubes)
ingredients.name: / 7 tbsp  unsalted butter (, unsalted, softened, cut into 1cm / 0.4" cubes)

ingredients.item: egg (, at room temperature (~50 - 55g/2 oz) (Note 3))
ingredients.name: egg (, at room temperature (~50 - 55g/2 oz) (Note 3))

instructions: Mix dry ingredients, rub in butter then egg (or use food processor). Form disc, fridge 30 min. Portion into 6 balls*, roll out 15 cm / 6.5" round (~3mm / 1/8" thick), line 6 tartlet tins, trim excess. Fridge 30 min. Blind bake 12 min at 200°C / 390°F (180°C fan) with weights + 5 min uncovered for par-baked. * For mini tins or muffin tin, roll out single large one and press out circles. Gather scraps and repeat.

By hand option - Mix together flour, icing sugar, salt and almond meal in a bowl. Add butter and use your fingertips to rub it in until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add egg, mix with a rubber spatula until it becomes too hard to stir anymore, then use your hands to bring it together into a dough.

Food processor (30 sec) - Using the standard metal S blade, pulse the flour, icing sugar, salt and almond meal once just to combine. Add butter and pulse 3 to 4 times until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add egg and blitz for 15 to 20 seconds until it comes together into a dough.

Fridge 30 min - Turn dough out from the bowl or food processor onto a work surface. Knead lightly just to bring together into a smooth ball. Flatten into a 2cm / 0.8" thick disc. Wrap with cling wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Divide dough (for larger tartlet tins) - Cut the disc into 6 equal portions, or however many tartlet tins you are using, then roll into balls. (If using a muffin tin or lots of mini tart tins, don't portion, roll out one big sheet, press circles out and press into tin. See Note 4)
Roll each ball out into a 15 cm / 6.5" round (~3mm / 1/8" thick).

Line and trim - Press pastry into 6 tartlet tins (12cm / 4.7"), taking care not to stretch the dough as this causes shrinkage during baking. Roll the rolling pin over the tartlet tin to trim excess dough. (No need to grease the tins even if they are not non-stick ones, the butter in the pastry essentially self-greases the tins - as reader Ali so succinctly explained!).
Prick the base of the pastry 10 times with a fork. Not all the way through - just make a light prick on the surface. (Do less pricks for smaller tarts).
Refrigerate 30 minutes - Put the pastry in the tart tin for 30 minutes. (Extra insurance policy to avoid shrinkage and walls sliding down).
Preheat oven to 200°C / 390°F (180°C fan-forced).

Baking beads - Cut or tear baking paper into pieces about 50% larger than the tart shells. Scrunch the paper in your fist then unravel, smooth out and fit into the tartlet tins (scrunching makes it fit in more easily into the corners). Fill with baking beads (or dry raw rice or beans).

Park-bake or fully baked? Par-bake if the tartlet shell will be baked again after filling (eg. almond cream / frangipane like Raspberry Tartlets). Fully bake if they will not be baked again (eg filling with pastry cream or whipped cream).

Par-baked (12 + 5 min) - Bake 12 minutes. Use paper overhang to remove the beads, then bake uncovered for 5 minutes. Pastry should pale golden on the base and light golden on the edges. It will go golden when the filled pastry is baked.
Fully baked (14 + 5 min) - Bake 15 minutes, remove beads, then bake 5 minutes uncovered. The base should be light golden and the edges should be golden.
Cool and fill - Fully cool in the tart tins before filling and baking again if filling needs to be cooked (like Raspberry Tartlets).
Storage - Or keep unfilled in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

instructions: Tenderise beef - toss with baking soda, leave 20 min, rinse, season with soy sauce.
Stir fry - Sauté onion first, then beef, then garlic, then stems. Add leafy greens, prepared noodles, and sauce. Toss well then serve.
Tenderise - Sprinkle the beef with baking soda in a small bowl. Toss with your fingertips to coat, separating the beef slices. Leave for 20 minutes to tenderise.

Rinse, dry, season - Rinse in a colander, shake and pat off excess water with a paper towel (no need to be thorough). Place in a bowl and toss with the soy sauce. Set aside. (It doesn't need marinating time).
Sauce - Mix ingredients in a small bowl.

Soak and rinse noodles - Prepare the noodles according to packet directions (usually soaking in boiling water for 5 - 10 minutes). Drain, then rinse under tap water to remove excess starch so it doesn't go gluey when cooked.

Cook onion, beef then garlic - Heat the oil over high heat in a large wok or large deep fry pan / skillet (~30cm/12"). Add the onion for 30 seconds. Add beef and cook until the red is almost gone (~1 minute), then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

Stems then everything else - Add the stem part of the Asian greens, toss for 1 minute. Add the leafy part, noodles then sauce (in that order). Toss for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes until the sauce has stained all the noodles and there is no sauce left in the base of the pan.  Serve immediately!

ingredients.name: / 5.6oz x 2   snapper fillets (, skin off, pin boned (or other fish fillets, see Note 1))

ingredients.item: extra virgin olive oil (, separated)
ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil (, separated)

ingredients.name: / 7oz  kipfler potatoes (fingerling potatoes) (, peeled and sliced 0.5cm / 0.2" thick - 2 medium (or baby potatoes))

ingredients.name: zucchini (, sliced 0.5cm / 0.2" thick)

ingredients.name: red capsicum (bell pepper) (, cut in half, cored then sliced 0.5cm / 0.2" thick)

ingredients.name: red onion (, cut into wedges 0.3cm / 0.1" thick)

ingredients.name: dill sprigs ((Note 2))

ingredients.name: chardonnay or other dry white wine (, (sub low-sodium vegetable stock/broth) (Note 3))

ingredients.item: Lemon wedges
ingredients.name: Lemon wedges

instructions: Pre-heat oven to 190°C / 375°F (170°C fan). Sauté potatoes for 4 min, then add remaining vegetables, salt, pepper and toss briefly. Divide vegetables between parcels, top with seasoned fish, dill, oil and wine. Seal the parcels and bake 18 min, then rest 3 min before opening.
Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F (170°C fan-forced).

Cook potato - Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and cook for 4 minutes, stirring regularly (use 2 wooden spoons if needed). They should pick up a little colour but not too much.
Cook the rest of vegetables - Add the zucchini, capsicum, red onion, garlic and half of the salt and pepper. Toss everything together for about 1 minute, then set aside.

Place two pieces of foil on your work surface (50cm / 20" long x 30cm / 12" wide), then top with a sheet of baking paper/parchment paper (40cm / 16" x 30cm / 12"). Divide the vegetables between the two, placing them in the middle. (Note 4)
Fish - Pat the snapper fillets dry, season both side with the remaining salt and pepper, then place on top of the vegetables.
Place 3 dill sprigs on top of each fish. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and pour 1 tbsp of white wine over each.

Build the parcels (video is helpful here) - Bring the short edges of the foil and baking paper together and fold over twice to seal that side. Press down gently along the fold to flatten it. Then, working on one end, fold each corner in to form a triangle, then fold that triangle over twice more to lock in the seal. Repeat on the other end so both ends are sealed the same way. Redo the same with the other parcel.
Bake & rest - Place the parcels on a baking tray and cook for 18 minutes. Remove and let rest for 3 minutes. (Once cooked, the core fish temperature should read at least 55°C / 130°F.)
Serving - Grand opening time! Open the parcels, watch the steam escape, squeeze some lemon juice over and eat while hot with some crusty bread on the side.
